title: Optimal size of weak \(\varepsilon\)-nets for convex ranges
formal: For each fixed dimension d, what is the asymptotic minimum worst-case size, as a function of epsilon, of a weak epsilon-net for a finite point set in \(R^{d}\) with respect to all convex ranges?

sentences: A weak \(\varepsilon\)-net places auxiliary points so that every convex set containing at least an \(\varepsilon\) fraction of a given point set contains an auxiliary point.
The auxiliary points may lie anywhere in the ambient Euclidean space.
For each fixed dimension, the task is to determine the smallest worst-case net size as \(\varepsilon\) decreases.
The challenge comes from hitting all sufficiently populated convex regions simultaneously, regardless of the original configuration.
Sharp bounds would quantify how economically a finite set can represent its large convex subsets.
